links.outcome: De-identification F1 of fine-tuned vs non-fine-tuned and prompt-based models on local real-world data
links.effect: Models without fine-tuning and prompt-based LLMs had macro-F1 0.14 to 0.5 on ObstEHR; fine-tuned models reached up to 0.956.
links.quote: Fine-tuned models achieved higher performance, reaching macro-averaged F1 scores of up to 0.956.

links.outcome: Accuracy of automated de-identification of Spanish clinical text by non-fine-tuned and prompt-based models
links.effect: Non-fine-tuned and prompt-based LLM approaches gave macro-F1 of 0.14 to 0.5 on ObstEHR and 0.19 to 0.5 on MEDDOCAN, leaving inadequate de-identification.
links.quote: Models without fine-tuning and prompt-based LLMs showed limited performance, with macro-averaged F1 scores ranging from 0.14 to 0.5 on ObstEHR and from 0.19 to 0.5 on MEDDOCAN.

unlisted_practices: Fine-tuning task-specific models on annotated local data for de-identification, with learning-curve analysis of the training data needed

screen.reason: Evaluates different model strategies (prompting vs fine-tuning) on clinical text de-identification benchmark datasets; compares model performance rather than evaluating an organizational deployment practice or guardrail.
